answer: Min-cut attestation quorum: each identity holds one vote per social-graph min-cut, so clones behind one cut collapse into a single voice. Entry requires cross-cluster attestations; each new cut crossed demands its own disjoint attestors, so a jetty gate only opens once distinct clusters vouch. Clones therefore cannot reuse early trust: every sparrow needs a separate branch, every crossing a fresh canyon of unshared attestors. Cost grows quadratically in N since attestor sets fail together.
